mainTopic: The source that שחיטה is at the neck, how many סימנים animals, birds and fish need, and the view that a bird needs no שחיטה מן התורה
overview: The גמרא first explains that the extra mention of פדר teaches the כהן to cover the cut neck with the fat when he brings the head up to the מזבח, out of respect. It then brings a ברייתא on 'זאת תורת הבהמה והעוף'. One view learns that a bird, like an animal, needs שחיטה, and the word 'זאת' keeps a bird from needing רוב שנים. רבי אליעזר learns from the same פסוק that an animal, like a bird, is made fit at the neck, though not from the back of the neck. For him, 'זאת' teaches that an animal still needs two סימנים. בר קפרא says a bird needs one סימן because the פסוק places it between animals (two סימנים) and fish (no שחיטה). The גמרא proves that fish need no שחיטה from the word 'gathered'. A teaching ties this to creation: land creatures need two, water creatures none, and birds, made from mud, one. A story about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and an officer discusses whether birds came from water, land or mud. Finally רבי יצחק בן פנחס says a bird needs no שחיטה מן התורה, because the Torah only says 'ושפך'. The גמרא defends this view and begins testing it with challenges about כסוי הדם, which continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the Torah mention the fat a first time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the other mention of פדר comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first 'fat' that the Torah wrote, why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the word פדר shows up twice in the פסוקים about the עולה. It asks what the other mention is there to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One mention of פדר was already used to teach that שחיטה is at the neck. A rule in the גמרא is that no word in the Torah is extra, so the other mention needs its own lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat of the animal that is burned on the מזבח
The first one
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
'Why do I need it?' Asks why a word or teaching seems extra

phrases.english: And the first 'fat' that the Merciful One wrote,
phrases.notes: This is ויקרא 1:8. פדר comes up again in ויקרא 1:12.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפֶדֶר קַמָּא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the earlier derivation, before this section begins, that used ראש ופדר to show שחיטה is at the neck.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the other, seemingly extra mention of פדר teaches.

steps.title: The fat covers the cut neck out of respect
steps.stepSummary: The other mention of פדר teaches that the כהן covers the place of the cut with the fat when he brings the head up to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: How does he do it? He covers the place of slaughter with the fat and brings it up, and this is a respectful way toward the One Above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this mention of פדר teaches a practical detail of the עבודה. The כהן covers the bloody, cut neck with the fat as he carries the head up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is not extra after all. It teaches how the head is brought up, with the cut neck hidden under the fat. Bringing it up uncovered would not be respectful toward ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is needed for', which gives the word its own purpose
Covers
The place on the neck where the cut was made
A respectful manner
Of the One Above, meaning ה׳

phrases.english: It is needed for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
How does he (the כהן) do it?

phrases.aramaic: חוֹפֶה אֶת הַפֶּדֶר עַל בֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה וּמַעֲלֵהוּ,
phrases.english: He covers the place of slaughter with the fat and brings it up,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the head, which he brings up onto the מזבח.

phrases.english: and this is a respectful way toward the One Above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The other mention of פדר teaches that the fat covers the cut neck when the head is brought up, out of respect.

steps.title: Another תנא learns the neck rule from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a ברייתא in which a תנא learns that שחיטה is at the neck from 'זאת תורת הבהמה והעוף'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא brings it from here, as a ברייתא teaches: 'This is the law of the animal and of the bird.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new source for the rule that שחיטה is at the neck. It quotes the opening פסוק of a ברייתא, and the discussion of that פסוק follows in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the source was ראש ופדר. Here a different תנא uses a פסוק that puts בהמה and עוף together, which hints that their laws are compared. Exactly what is compared gets worked out next.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period
'Brings it from here': learns the rule from this source
'The law of the animal and the bird', a פסוק that groups the two together

phrases.english: And this תנא brings it from here,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule that שחיטה is done at the neck. The תנא meant is רבי אליעזר, who comes at the end.

phrases.english: as it is taught: 'This is the law of the animal and of the bird,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:46

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the פדר discussion and brings a different source for the neck rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברייתא sees the פסוק grouping בהמה and עוף as a source for how they are slaughtered.

steps.title: Animals and birds have very different טומאה laws
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how בהמה and עוף can be equal, since their laws of טומאת נבלה are opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what law is an animal equal to a bird, and a bird to an animal? An animal makes things impure by touching and carrying, and a bird does not. A bird makes clothing impure when it is in the throat, and an animal does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the idea that the פסוק makes animals and birds equal. In the laws of טומאה it finds two ways they are opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead animal's נבלה makes a person impure by touching it or carrying it, but a bird's נבלה does not. A kosher bird's נבלה makes a person and his clothes impure only when he swallows it, and an animal's נבלה does not work that way. So the פסוק cannot mean they are equal in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is equal to
Touching
Carrying
The throat, at the moment of swallowing
Makes the clothes of the person impure

steps.confusionAlert: 'בית הבליעה' does not mean the bird makes the throat impure. It means that eating a kosher bird's נבלה makes the eater, and the clothes he is wearing, impure at the moment he swallows it.

phrases.english: But in what law is it equal,
an animal to a bird and a bird to an animal?
An animal makes impure by touching and by carrying,
phrases.notes: This is the טומאה of a נבלה, an animal that died without proper שחיטה.

phrases.english: while a bird does not make impure by touching or by carrying!
A bird makes clothing impure when it is in the throat,

phrases.aramaic: בְּהֵמָה אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה בְּגָדִים אַבֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה!
phrases.english: while an animal does not make clothing impure when it is in the throat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי בְּאֵיזוֹ תּוֹרָה שָׁוְותָה בְּהֵמָה לָעוֹף וְעוֹף לִבְהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison suggested by the פסוק in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the פסוק makes בהמה and עוף equal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In טומאת נבלה they are opposites (touching and carrying versus swallowing), so there seems to be no area in which they are equal.

steps.title: Both need שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the comparison teaches that a bird, like an animal, is made permitted through שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what law are they equal? To tell you: just as an animal is through שחיטה, so too a bird is through שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats its question and gives the answer. The comparison is about שחיטה, not טומאה: a bird needs שחיטה just as an animal does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though their טומאה laws differ, both escape the status of נבלה only through שחיטה. This finds a real area where the פסוק makes them equal.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To tell you': introduces what the פסוק comes to teach
Kosher slaughter by cutting the throat
'Just as ... so too': a comparison of two cases

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֵיזוֹ תּוֹרָה שָׁוְותָה בְּהֵמָה לְעוֹף וְעוֹף לִבְהֵמָה?
phrases.english: In what law is an animal equal to a bird and a bird to an animal?
To tell you: just as an animal is through slaughter,
so too a bird is through slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the comparison to a different area of law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to compare them in טומאה, where they differ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is about שחיטה: both are permitted through it.

steps.title: Should a bird then need most of both סימנים?
steps.stepSummary: If the comparison is complete, a bird would need most of two סימנים cut, just like an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there it is through most of two, here too it should be through most of two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison further. If a bird's שחיטה is like an animal's, a bird should also need most of both the windpipe and the food pipe cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's שחיטה needs most of both סימנים. A full comparison would make the same demand for a bird, even though a bird needs only most of one סימן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If, just as there': takes the comparison one step further
Most of both סימנים
The windpipe and the food pipe, which are cut in שחיטה

phrases.english: If so, just as there (an animal) it is through most of two,
phrases.notes: 'Two' means the two סימנים, the windpipe and the food pipe.

phrases.english: so too here (a bird), through most of two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison from step 5 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of a bird's שחיטה to an animal's
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two are equal in שחיטה, every detail should carry over, including the need for רוב שנים.

steps.title: The word 'זאת' limits the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The word 'זאת' shows that the comparison does not cover every detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'זאת' (this).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the word 'זאת' limits the comparison. A bird needs שחיטה, but not most of both סימנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זאת' points to one particular law and cuts back how far the comparison goes. So the basic need for שחיטה carries over to a bird, but the amount that must be cut does not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches': introduces a word in the פסוק as the answer
'This', a word that limits the comparison to one point

steps.whatToRemember: According to the first view in the ברייתא, 'זאת תורת הבהמה והעוף' teaches that a bird needs שחיטה like an animal. The word 'זאת' keeps the comparison from requiring רוב שנים for a bird.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'This.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A word in the פסוק limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison should carry over every detail, including רוב שנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זאת' limits it: a bird needs שחיטה, but not most of both סימנים.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: an animal, like a bird, is made fit at the neck
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the comparison the other way: just as a bird is made fit at the neck, so is an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: In what law is an animal equal to a bird and a bird to an animal? To tell you: just as a bird is made fit from the neck, so too an animal is made fit from the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives his own explanation of the comparison. The Torah says outright that a bird is done at the neck, and the פסוק carries that over to an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the comparison runs from the bird to the animal. The Torah says a bird offering is done at the neck (מליקה, ממול ערפו), and that tells us an animal's שחיטה is also at the neck. This is the 'other source' for the neck rule promised in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: What makes it fit and permitted (for a קרבן or for eating)
Neck
Pinching a bird offering's neck with the כהן's fingernail

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר is the תנא who learns that שחיטה is at the neck from 'זאת תורת הבהמה והעוף'. Since a bird is made fit at the neck, an animal is too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a second source, besides ראש ופדר, for the basic rule that שחיטה is done at the neck.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֵיזוֹ תּוֹרָה שָׁוְותָה בְּהֵמָה לְעוֹף וְעוֹף לִבְהֵמָה?
phrases.english: In what law is an animal equal to a bird and a bird to an animal?

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר לָךְ: מָה עוֹף הֶכְשֵׁרוֹ מִן הַצַּוָּאר,
phrases.english: To tell you: just as a bird, its fitness is from the neck,
phrases.notes: The Torah says this about bird offerings, which are done at the neck (ויקרא 5:8).

phrases.english: so too an animal, its fitness is from the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the same comparison from step 5, and delivers the neck source promised in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal, like a bird, is made fit through a cut at the neck.

steps.title: Should an animal also be cut from the back of the neck?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes רבי אליעזר's comparison further: if an animal is like a bird, maybe it should also be cut from the back of the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as a bird's מליקה is done from the back of the neck, an animal should also be slaughtered from the back of the neck!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's comparison by taking it one step further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said an animal is like a bird, since both are done at the neck. But a bird's מליקה is done from the back of the neck. If the comparison holds, an animal would also need to be cut from the back, and not from the throat.

keyTerms.meaning: Facing the back of the neck (the nape)
There, in the other case being compared
So too here

phrases.english: If so, just as there it is "adjacent to the nape,"
phrases.notes: 'There' means the bird, and 'here' means the animal.

phrases.english: so too here it should be "adjacent to the nape"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן ״מִמּוּל עוֹרֶף״, אַף כָּאן ״מִמּוּל עוֹרֶף״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison רבי אליעזר made in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's comparison of animal to bird.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is full, the place of cutting should match too, which would mean cutting from the back of the neck.

steps.title: Only the bird is cut from the back of the neck
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about מליקה says 'its head', which limits cutting from the back of the neck to the bird alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he shall pinch off its head facing its nape, and not separate it.' 'Its head' means this one's head is cut from the back, but not another one's head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק that limits cutting from the back of the neck to birds only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ראשו' (its head) in the פסוק of מליקה is read as a limit. It tells us that only the bird's head is done from the back. An animal, 'the other', is not, so the comparison stops there.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; introduces a source
Pinching the neck of a bird קרבן with the כהן's fingernail
And he shall not separate the head completely

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And he shall pinch off its head adjacent to its nape,
but shall not divide it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:8

phrases.english: the head of this one is adjacent to the nape,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל אַחַר מִמּוּל עוֹרֶף.
phrases.english: but the head of another is not adjacent to the nape.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the bird; 'another' is the animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וּמָלַק אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ מִמּוּל עׇרְפּוֹ וְלֹא יַבְדִּיל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in a פסוק narrows the comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison might mean an animal is also cut from the back of the neck.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ראשו' limits cutting from the back to birds only; an animal is not cut that way.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר learn from 'זאת'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אליעזר does with the word 'זאת', which the first opinion used to limit the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, what does he do with this word 'זאת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי אליעזר learns from the word 'זאת', since he does not use it the way the first opinion did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, the first opinion used 'זאת' to limit the comparison, so a bird does not need most of two סימנים like an animal. רבי אליעזר reads the comparison differently, so the גמרא wants to know what job 'זאת' does for him.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? What does he learn from it?
'This', the opening word of the פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer,
what does he do with this "This"?
phrases.notes: This points to 'זאת תורת הבהמה והעוף', the word the first opinion used back in step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הַאי ״זֹאת״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the word 'זאת' from step 7 and asks how רבי אליעזר uses it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אליעזר learns from the word 'זאת'.

steps.title: 'זאת' stops an animal from needing only one סימן
steps.stepSummary: Without 'זאת', one might think an animal, like a bird, needs only one סימן cut. 'זאת' blocks that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for 'זאת', I would have said: just as a bird needs one סימן, so too an animal needs one סימן. So the Torah wrote 'זאת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר also uses 'זאת' to limit the comparison, so an animal still needs both סימנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי אליעזר agrees the comparison cannot be total. Without 'זאת', we would copy the bird's rule of one סימן onto animals. 'זאת' teaches that an animal still needs two.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said; a mistaken first thought
One of the two signs cut in שחיטה: the windpipe or the food pipe
The Merciful One; a name for ה׳ as the Torah's Author

phrases.english: If not for "This," I would have said:
just as a bird is done with one siman,
so too an animal is done with one siman;
therefore the Merciful One wrote "This."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זאת' prevents us from learning that an animal needs only one סימן like a bird.

steps.title: בר קפרא: a bird sits between animal and fish, so it needs one סימן
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists the bird between animals and fish, so a bird gets a middle rule: one סימן, not two and not zero.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: 'This is the law of the animal and the bird.' The פסוק placed the bird between animals and fish. It cannot need two סימנים, because it is compared to fish. It cannot need nothing, because it is compared to animals. So how is it made fit? With one סימן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings בר קפרא's teaching, which gives a source that a bird needs one סימן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the bird is listed between animals, which need two סימנים, and fish, which need no שחיטה. Because it is compared to both, it takes the middle path. It needs one סימן, which is more than fish and less than animals.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק placed
It was compared to, through a הֶקֵּשׁ
What makes it fit and permitted to eat
It is impossible

steps.whatToRemember: A bird needs one סימן because the Torah places it between animals (two סימנים) and fish (no שחיטה).

phrases.english: Bar Kappara teaches:
"This is the law of the animal and of the bird"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:46. The פסוק goes on to mention creatures of the water, meaning fish.

phrases.english: The verse placed the bird
between animal and fish.
To require it to have two simanim cut is impossible,
since it was already compared to fish;
to exempt it with nothing at all is impossible,
since it was already compared to an animal.
So how is it made fit?
With one siman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about the source for a bird's שחיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird is made fit by cutting one סימן, because it is placed between animals and fish.

steps.title: How do we know fish need no שחיטה?
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא assumed fish need no שחיטה. The גמרא asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fish do not need שחיטה. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of an idea בר קפרא relied on: that fish need no שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא's whole argument depends on fish needing nothing at all. If that is not proven, the 'middle path' for birds falls apart, so the גמרא wants a clear source.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that need שחיטה
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Fish, that they are not subject to slaughter,
from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּגִים דְּלָאו בְּנֵי שְׁחִיטָה נִינְהוּ, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that fish do not need שחיטה.

steps.title: First suggestion: fish only need to be gathered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a פסוק where animals are 'slaughtered' but fish are only 'gathered', which would show fish need no שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because it is written: 'Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered for them', which shows that just gathering is enough for fish...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a source: fish are 'gathered' rather than 'slaughtered'. The next step challenges this proof, and step 17 defends it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, animals are 'slaughtered' but fish are 'gathered'. This seems to show that fish only need to be caught and not slaughtered. The גמרא will test this proof against the quail, and in the end it keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; a suggestion that will likely be rejected
Gathering
It is enough

steps.confusionAlert: 'אילימא' means 'if you would say', and the גמרא pushes back on it in the next step. But here the proof survives: step 17 shows why it holds.

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is written:
"If flocks and herds be slaughtered for them

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֶת כׇּל דְּגֵי הַיָּם יֵאָסֵף לָהֶם״,
phrases.english: or if all the fish of the sea be gathered for them,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:22

phrases.english: meaning mere gathering is enough for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggested source: in במדבר 11:22, fish are 'gathered' rather than 'slaughtered', so gathering alone is enough. It is challenged in step 16 and upheld in step 17.

steps.title: Quail are also 'gathered'. Do they also need no slaughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the 'gathering' proof: the תורה says quail were 'gathered' too, yet birds cannot be fully exempt from שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the תורה says about quail 'they gathered the quail.' Should we say birds also need no שחיטה? But you yourself said a bird cannot be exempted with nothing, because it was already compared to animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 15. If 'gathering' means no שחיטה is needed, then quail, which were also 'gathered', would need no שחיטה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 learned from the word 'gathered' that fish need no שחיטה. Quail are described with the same word. But step 13 already said a bird needs at least one סימן, because the פסוק places it next to animals. So the proof seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if that is so'. It opens a challenge by showing where the reasoning would lead.
Quail, the birds that fell in the desert
Gathering
It was compared or placed side by side with something in the פסוק (a היקש)

phrases.english: But if that is so,
regarding quail, about which it is written:
"And they gathered the quail,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:32

phrases.english: would you say so too, that they are not made fit by slaughter?
But didn't you say:
To exempt it with nothing at all is impossible,
since it was already compared to an animal!
phrases.notes: This points back to step 13: the bird sits next to animals in the פסוק, so it needs at least one סימן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof offered in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'gathering' that fish need no שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word is used for quail. If it meant 'no שחיטה', birds would need none, which clashes with the rule in step 13 that birds need one סימן.

steps.title: For fish, 'gathering' replaces slaughter
steps.stepSummary: Only by fish is 'gathering' written in place of the slaughter mentioned for other animals. By quail it is just a description.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, by the quail, 'gathering' is not written in place of the slaughter of other creatures. Here, by the fish, 'gathering' is written in place of the slaughter of other creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its proof. The word 'gather' only teaches 'no שחיטה' when it stands in the spot where other creatures are 'slaughtered'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the fish פסוק, flocks and herds are 'slaughtered' while fish are 'gathered'. That contrast shows gathering takes the place of slaughter. By the quail there is no such contrast, so 'gathered' just describes collecting them.

keyTerms.meaning: In place of, instead of
Of others, here meaning the flocks and herds

steps.whatToRemember: Fish need no שחיטה because the פסוק says 'gather' for fish exactly where it says 'slaughter' for animals.

phrases.english: There, gathering is not written
in place of the slaughter of others;
here, gathering is written
in place of the slaughter of others.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the fish פסוק from step 15, where flocks and herds are 'slaughtered' but fish are 'gathered'.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא כְּתִיבָא אֲסִיפָה בִּמְקוֹם שְׁחִיטָה דְּאַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the context of the two פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any 'gathering' in the תורה means no שחיטה is needed, so quail too
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'gathering' written in place of others' slaughter teaches an exemption, and that happens only by fish

steps.title: Animals from land, fish from water, birds from mud
steps.stepSummary: עובר גלילאה ties each creature's rule to what it was created from: land means two סימנים, water means none, mud means one.
steps.simpleTranslation: A passerby from the גליל taught: an animal, created from dry land, is made fit by two סימנים. Fish, created from water, are made fit with nothing. A bird, created from mud, is made fit by one סימן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching gives a reason for the three rules. Each creature's rule matches the material it was created from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a second way to see the middle rule for birds from step 13. Mud is part land and part water, so the bird gets a rule halfway between the animal's two סימנים and the fish's zero.

keyTerms.meaning: A passerby from the Galil, an unnamed teacher
What makes it fit (kosher) to eat
Dry land
Mud or marshy ground, a mix of earth and water
Nothing at all

steps.whatToRemember: Land creature means two סימנים. Water creature means none. Bird, from mud, means one.

phrases.english: A passerby from the Galil expounded:
An animal, which was created from dry land:
it is made fit by two סימנים;
fish, which were created from water:
they are made fit with nothing;
a bird, which was created from mud:
it is made fit by one סימן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another reason for the three rules discussed in steps 13 to 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: How many סימנים a creature needs matches what it was created from: land two, water none, mud one.

steps.title: Birds have fish-like scales on their feet
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל קפוטקאה supports the mud idea: birds have scales on their legs like fish, so they are partly water creatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל קפוטקאה said: Know that this is true, for birds have scales on their feet like fish.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא brings a proof from nature that birds came partly from water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If birds were purely land creatures, why would they have fish-like scales? The scales show a water connection, which fits the claim that birds came from mud, a mix of land and water.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Know that it is so', a phrase that introduces supporting evidence
Scales

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel of Cappadocia said:
Know that this is so,
for birds have scales
on their feet, like fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the teaching of step 18
steps.raayaObject: That birds were created from mud, part land and part water
steps.raayaSupportSource: The physical fact that birds have scales on their legs, like fish

steps.title: Two פסוקים disagree on where birds came from
steps.stepSummary: A questioner points out that one פסוק says birds came from the water, and another says they came from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also asked him: One פסוק says 'Let the waters swarm with living creatures, and birds will fly', so birds came from water. Another פסוק says 'God formed from the ground every beast of the field and every bird of the sky', so birds came from land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about where birds were created. A questioner sets two פסוקים against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בראשית 1 places the birds in the water creation, while בראשית 2 lists them among things formed from the ground. This is a classic contradiction between two פסוקים, and it connects to the 'mud' idea just taught.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he also asked him', showing this is part of a longer conversation
'One פסוק says'. This opens a contradiction between פסוקים.
Apparently, so we see

steps.confusionAlert: The text does not name the people here. This line comes from a longer conversation between a Roman official (the questioner) and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי (the one answering).

phrases.english: And furthermore he asked him:
One verse says:
"And God said: Let the waters swarm
with swarms of living creatures, and birds will fly,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:20

phrases.english: so apparently they were created from water;
and it is written:
"And the Lord God formed from the ground

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה וְאֵת כׇּל עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם״,
phrases.english: every beast of the field and every bird of the sky,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:19

phrases.english: so apparently they were created from land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story connected to the 'mud' idea of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the creation פסוקים about birds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says birds came from water, another says from the ground. Both cannot be true.

steps.title: The answer to the questioner: from mud
steps.stepSummary: The questioner is told birds came from mud, which fits both פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They were created from mud.
steps.whatsHappening: The sage answers the questioner that birds came from mud. Mud is both water and earth, so both פסוקים are true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the view of עובר גלילאה in step 18. Mud mixes the two materials, so it settles the contradiction in a simple way.

keyTerms.meaning: They were created

phrases.english: He said to him: They were created from mud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combines the two sources: mud is both water and land
steps.terutzMaskana: Birds came from mud, so both פסוקים are partly right

steps.title: The real answer to the students: from water
steps.stepSummary: Seeing his students puzzled, the sage admits the mud answer was weak. Birds came from water. The second פסוק mentions them only because they were brought to אדם to be named.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw his students looking at each other. He said to them: Does it bother you that I pushed off my enemy with a piece of straw? Really, birds were created from water. So why does the פסוק say He brought them to אדם? So that he would give them names.
steps.whatsHappening: The sage gives his students the true answer. Birds came from water, and the second פסוק lists them only because they were brought to אדם for naming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mud answer was a quick way to send away a hostile questioner. The real answer reads בראשית 2 differently: the birds are mentioned there for the naming, not to say they were formed from the ground. So the first פסוק (water) is the true source.

keyTerms.meaning: I pushed off, I sent away
With straw, meaning with a flimsy answer
To give them names

steps.whatToRemember: The quick answer was 'mud'. The real answer is that birds came from water, and בראשית 2 mentions them only because אדם named them.
steps.confusionAlert: This story ends with birds coming from water, not mud. Do not mix that up with the 'mud' teaching of עובר גלילאה in step 18.

phrases.english: He saw his students
looking at one another;
he said to them:
Is it troubling in your eyes
that I pushed off my enemy with straw?
phrases.notes: 'Straw' means a flimsy answer, good enough to send away someone who isn't really looking to learn.

phrases.english: They were created from water.
And why did He bring them to the man?
phrases.notes: He means: why are birds listed in בראשית 2:19 at all? That same פסוק goes on to say they were brought to אדם.

phrases.english: So that he would give them names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the quick answer of step 21 with the true resolution
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the second פסוק so it no longer speaks about what birds were made from
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Birds came from mud, a blend of the two פסוקים
steps.terutzMaskana: Birds came from water. בראשית 2 mentions them only because they were brought to אדם to be named.

steps.title: A second version: water for the officer, mud for the students
steps.stepSummary: Some say the sage gave the officer the 'water' answer, and gave his students the 'mud' answer because of the פסוק 'ויצר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it went the other way. He told the officer the other answer (birds came from water). He told his students the first answer (birds came from mud), because the פסוק 'ויצר' says birds were formed from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the story from steps 21-22. In this version, the mud answer is the real one, and the water answer was only for the officer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, the sage told his students the mud answer was weak and that birds came from water. This version flips it: the water answer was for the outsider, and the mud answer was for the students. The reason is the פסוק of 'ויצר', which lists birds among the things formed from the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: A government officer or ruler
Another version or wording of the answer
'And He formed', the פסוק saying creatures were formed from the ground

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the story. In the first, the real answer is water. In the second, the real answer is mud, because of the פסוק 'ויצר'.

phrases.english: And some say: with the other answer
phrases.notes: The 'other answer' is the one about water, from step 22.

phrases.english: he spoke to that officer,
and with the first answer
phrases.notes: The 'first answer' is the mud answer, from step 21.

phrases.english: he spoke to his students,
because it is written about them in 'And He formed'.
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:19

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: בְּלָשׁוֹן אַחֵר אָמַר לְאוֹתוֹ הֶגְמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the story told in step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 22 had the sage dropping the mud answer and going with water.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this version, mud is the real answer, given to the students, because of the פסוק 'ויצר'. Water was the answer given to the officer.

steps.title: Birds need no שחיטה from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רבי יצחק בן פנחס: birds do not need שחיטה מן התורה, because the פסוק only says 'ושפך', just spill the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רבי יצחק בן פנחס: from the Torah, a bird does not need שחיטה. The פסוק says 'he shall spill', so simply spilling its blood is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about birds. A sage says that, from the Torah, a bird does not need proper שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word 'ושפך', 'and he shall spill', in the פסוק about a person who traps a חיה or עוף. Since the Torah speaks only of spilling the blood, any way of spilling it would be enough from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher slaughter by cutting the throat in the proper way
From the Torah itself, not from the רבנן
'And he shall spill', the word the proof is built on
Simply is enough
Bird

steps.confusionAlert: This is one sage's view about the Torah level. The גמרא now goes on to test it with questions.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן פִּנְחָס:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak ben Pinchas:
A bird does not need slaughter by Torah law,
as it says: 'And he shall spill'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:13

phrases.english: Simply spilling its blood is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן פִּנְחָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new legal topic about birds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the Torah, a bird needs only to have its blood spilled, not proper שחיטה.

steps.title: Then a חיה should be the same
steps.stepSummary: If 'ושפך' means spilling is enough, the same should apply to a חיה, which is in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a חיה should also need only spilling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 24. The same פסוק talks about a חיה too, so a חיה should also need no שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of 'ושפך' covers both a חיה and an עוף that a person traps. If the word 'ושפך' removes the need for שחיטה, it should remove it for both.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
A wild (undomesticated) animal, like a deer

phrases.english: If so, an undomesticated animal too!
phrases.notes: He means a חיה should also need only spilling, since it is in the same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of step 24.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same פסוק includes a חיה, so the proof should free a חיה from שחיטה too. Yet a חיה does need שחיטה.

steps.title: A חיה is compared to פסולי המוקדשין
steps.stepSummary: A חיה is linked by a הקש to blemished קדשים animals, which need שחיטה, so it needs שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חיה is compared to פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 25. A חיה needs שחיטה because the Torah compares it to disqualified קדשים animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין are holy animals that became unfit for the מזבח and are eaten after פדיון, and they need שחיטה. Because of the הקש, a חיה gets the same need for שחיטה, even though 'ושפך' is written about it. The source for this הקש is explained later in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is compared, linked by a הקש (a Torah comparison)
Holy animals that became unfit for the מזבח

phrases.english: It is compared to disqualified consecrated animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate source (a הקש) requires שחיטה for a חיה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חיה should need only spilling, like a bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: A הקש to פסולי המוקדשין requires שחיטה for a חיה.

steps.title: Birds are also compared to בהמה
steps.stepSummary: Birds are also linked to בהמה by the פסוק 'זאת תורת הבהמה והעוף', so birds should need שחיטה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bird is also compared to a בהמה, as it is written: 'This is the law of the animal and the bird'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back using the same kind of answer. If a הקש makes a חיה need שחיטה, a different הקש should make a bird need it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts בהמה and עוף together in one 'תורה', one law. Since a בהמה needs שחיטה, the bird should need it as well, so the rule of step 24 seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A domesticated animal, like a cow or sheep
'The law of the animal and the bird', a פסוק joining them

phrases.english: A bird too is compared to a domesticated animal,
as it is written: 'This is the law of the animal and of the bird'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:46

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the method of step 26's answer to challenge step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that birds need no שחיטה מן התורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a הקש can make a חיה need שחיטה, then the הקש of עוף to בהמה should make a bird need it too.

steps.title: But 'ושפך את דמו' is written
steps.stepSummary: The clear word 'ושפך' in the פסוק tells us a bird needs only spilling, even though there is a הקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'He shall spill its blood'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 27. The Torah directly says 'he shall spill its blood', so that word decides the bird's law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the bird, two sources pull in different directions: the הקש to בהמה, and the word 'ושפך'. The גמרא says 'ושפך' is the one that tells us about the bird. That brings up the next question: why does 'ושפך' go on the bird and not on the חיה?

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written
Its blood

phrases.english: But it is written: 'He shall spill its blood'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A clear פסוק decides against the הקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הקש to בהמה should make a bird need שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ושפך' is written, so a bird needs only spilling.

steps.title: Why put 'ושפך' on the bird and not the חיה?
steps.stepSummary: Each creature has a הקש, so why should the word 'ושפך' free the bird and not the חיה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you apply it to the bird? Apply it to the חיה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how the word 'ושפך' was used. Both a חיה and an עוף are in the פסוק, so why does the bird get the 'spilling is enough' rule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both creatures have a הקש saying they need שחיטה: the חיה to פסולי המוקדשין, and the bird to בהמה. One word, 'ושפך', cancels the need for one of them. The גמרא asks why we chose the bird and not the חיה.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why did you choose this way?)
You cast, meaning you applied the rule to

phrases.english: And what did you see
that you cast it upon the bird?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the lesson of 'ושפך', that spilling alone is enough.

phrases.english: Cast it upon the undomesticated animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי חָזֵית דְּשָׁדֵית לֵיהּ עַל עוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 28 used 'ושפך' for the bird.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying 'ושפך' to the bird rather than the חיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both creatures are in the פסוק and both have a הקש, so there seems to be no reason to pick the bird.

steps.title: The bird is mentioned last, right before 'ושפך'
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense to apply 'ושפך' to the bird, because the פסוק ends with the bird just before it says 'ושפך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense, because the פסוק ended with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 29. The bird is the last thing named before 'ושפך', so the word goes on the bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'a חיה or עוף that may be eaten, and he shall spill its blood'. The word closest to 'ושפך' is עוף, so the lesson goes on the bird. This keeps the rule of step 24: a bird needs no שחיטה מן התורה, while a חיה does because of its הקש.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is logical
It ended with it (the last thing mentioned)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יצחק בן פנחס, a bird needs no שחיטה מן התורה, because of 'ושפך', which is written right after the bird. A חיה does need שחיטה, because of its הקש to פסולי המוקדשין.

phrases.english: It stands to reason, because the verse ended with it.
phrases.notes: The פסוק names the bird last, just before 'he shall spill its blood'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ושפך' could just as well go on the חיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It goes on the bird, which is named last, right before 'ושפך'.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming challenges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives three key words to help remember the upcoming challenges about birds and שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: became a נבלה, blood, through מליקה.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא lists three short words to help us remember the order of the challenges that are coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one coming source: 'became a נבלה' is the first challenge, 'blood' is the ברייתא about needing the blood, and 'מליקה' is a later one. It teaches no law itself; it is a map of what follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of key words to remember a series of teachings
Killing a bird by pinching its neck with the fingernail, as done with bird offerings

phrases.english: (A memory aid:
became a carcass, blood, through pinching.)
phrases.notes: Each word is a reminder of one of the challenges coming up, in order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source for the view was settled, the גמרא prepares a series of challenges against it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; a memory list for the coming challenges.

steps.title: Stabbing exempts from covering, so it cannot be a bird's real שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that one who stabs or rips is exempt from covering the blood. If a bird needs no Torah שחיטה, stabbing a bird should count as its שחיטה and require covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who slaughters and it becomes a נבלה in his hand, or one who stabs or rips, is exempt from covering the blood. But if you say a bird has no שחיטה from the Torah, then stabbing it is its שחיטה, so it should need covering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to attack the view that a bird needs no שחיטה from the Torah. The משנה says stabbing exempts from covering, which seems to clash with that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כסוי הדם applies only when the killing makes the creature fit to eat. The משנה says stabbing (נחירה) does not do that, so no covering is needed. But if a bird needs only spilling of blood from the Torah, stabbing a bird would make it fit, and covering should be required.

keyTerms.meaning: It became a נבלה (an improperly killed animal) in his hand because the שחיטה was invalid
One who stabs or slices the neck instead of slaughtering properly
One who rips out the windpipe or food pipe
The מצוה to cover the blood of a slaughtered חיה or bird
Exempt from covering the blood

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who slaughters and it became a carcass in his hand,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in this מסכת, about covering the blood.

phrases.english: one who stabs and one who rips –
is exempt from covering.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֵין שְׁחִיטָה לָעוֹף מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: And if you say there is no slaughter for a bird by Torah law,
its stabbing is its slaughter,
let it require covering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first challenge from the memory list ('became a נבלה'), attacking the view established in steps 28-30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a bird needs no שחיטה from the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts stabbing from covering. Under this view, stabbing a bird should count as valid killing, so the blood should need covering.

steps.title: The משנה is talking only about a חיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה about stabbing speaks only about a חיה, not a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think it is talking about a bird? No, it is talking about a חיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the משנה: its rule about stabbing refers to a חיה, not a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חיה needs real שחיטה from the Torah, so stabbing it is not valid and no covering is needed. A bird is not included in that rule, so the משנה does not contradict the view.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild (undomesticated) kosher animal, such as a deer
Do you think? (introduces a correction of how the questioner read the source)

phrases.english: Do you maintain it is about a bird?
No, it is about an undomesticated animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the source speaks only about a חיה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought the משנה covers birds too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deals only with a חיה, which needs real שחיטה, so the bird view stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא about someone who wants to keep the blood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one who slaughters and needs the blood must still cover it; to avoid covering, he should stab or rip instead. This sets up a new challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who slaughters and needs the blood is still obligated to cover it. What should he do? Either stab it or rip it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source (the 'blood' of the memory aid) to challenge the view again. This step quotes the ברייתא and sets up the challenge that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says stabbing or ripping is a way to escape covering, because such killing is not valid. If this ברייתא includes birds, it would again suggest stabbing is not valid for a bird, against the view that a bird needs no Torah שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Needs the blood for some use (so he does not want to cover it)
Obligated to cover the blood
How should he act? (asks for the practical way out)

steps.confusionAlert: Stabbing here is not presented as a good thing to do; it is mentioned only as a way the killing does not count, so the covering duty does not apply.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who slaughters and needs the blood –
is obligated to cover.
How does he act?
phrases.notes: He means: what can he do if he wants to keep the blood without covering it?

phrases.english: He either stabs it or rips it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, the גמרא brings the second source from the memory list ('blood').
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a bird needs no שחיטה from the Torah
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats stabbing as invalid killing that frees one from covering; if it includes birds, stabbing a bird would not be its שחיטה.
